title: Crispy Air Fryer Sweet Potato Cubes (Garlic Herb Crunch on a Budget)
description: Crispy air fryer sweet potato cubes tossed in garlic herb seasoning. Easy, budget-friendly 15-minute side dish for under 85 cents a serving.
storyHeading: How to Make This for a Fraction of Takeout Cost
story: My local burger counter charges $7.50 for a small basket of sweet potato bites. A three-pound bag of sweet potatoes at Aldi runs me $2.29, which means this full batch costs barely 80 cents per plate. In my first few test runs, though, my cubes turned into mushy, soft orange pillows. The culprit was excess moisture mixed with too much oil. The simple grocery-pantry fix: cut them into uniform half-inch dice, pat them completely dry with a tea towel, and toss them with one teaspoon of cornstarch before adding a single tablespoon of oil. The cornstarch grabs the exterior moisture and turns into a thin, shatter-crisp crust under the circulating heat of the air fryer basket.
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (about 1.5 lbs), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 tbsp olive oil or avocado oil
1/2 tsp dried Italian seasoning (or crushed oregano)
instructions: Pat the cut sweet potato cubes thoroughly dry using paper towels or a clean dish towel to eliminate surface wetness, then transfer to a medium bowl and toss with the cornstarch until no white powder remains visible.
Drizzle the olive oil over the cubes, then sprinkle in the garlic powder, dried Italian seasoning, kosher salt, and black pepper, tossing until every piece has a light, even sheen.
Preheat your air fryer to 390°F for 3 minutes, then dump the sweet potatoes into the basket in an even layer (work in two batches if using a compact basket under 4 quarts to avoid overcrowding).
Cook at 390°F for 13 to 15 minutes, vigorously shaking the basket every 4 to 5 minutes so the cubes brown on all sides and develop blistered edges while staying fork-tender inside.
proHack: Hold off on salting until the absolute last second before the cubes hit the basket. Salt draws moisture out of raw sweet potatoes almost immediately; if they sit salted on your counter for ten minutes while the fryer heats up, they will release water and steam rather than crisp.
servingIdea: Pair these alongside grilled smash burgers or spoon them into warm weeknight black bean bowls topped with chipotle mayo and pickled red onions.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight glass container in the fridge for up to 4 days. To bring back maximum crunch, re-crisp them in the air fryer at 380°F for 3 to 4 minutes instead of using the microwave.

faqs.question: Can I leave the sweet potato skins on?
faqs.answer: Yes. Just scrub the skins thoroughly under cold water and dry them completely before cutting. Skin-on cubes save five minutes of prep and add extra fiber and earthy flavor.

faqs.question: Why did my sweet potatoes turn out soft instead of crunchy?
faqs.answer: The basket was likely overloaded. When sweet potatoes sit stacked atop one another, trapped air turns to steam. Keep them in a single, spaced layer and shake every four minutes.
